objective.statement: Enumerate the option space as a morphological grid and mark every cell, so that a COMPLETENESS claim is backed by the grid rather than by effort.
objective.charter: Three parameterisers decompose the problem into independent parameters and must show them orthogonal; eight cell evaluators mark every cell of the resulting cross-product feasible, infeasible, or unknown; a methodologist polices the completeness claim. This is the only preset in the deep tier that can legitimately say 'we considered everything', and it earns that only because the grid is enumerable and every cell carries a mark. 'We worked hard and found nothing else' is not completeness.
success_criteria: the parameters are shown pairwise-orthogonal, not merely listed
every cell of the cross-product carries a feasible / infeasible / unknown mark
no cell is left unmarked - an unmarked cell falsifies the completeness claim
if no cell is feasible, the run returns a proof of impossibility rather than a forced pick

context.briefing: Try to COLLAPSE the parameter set. If two parameters co-vary, the grid is smaller than it looks and the completeness claim is inflated.
Refuse any completeness claim not backed by a fully marked grid. Count the cells yourself; do not accept a count you were told.

committees.mandate: Decompose into parameters and PROVE they are orthogonal. Deliverable: the axis list plus the pairwise-independence evidence.
Mark every cell of the cross-product feasible / infeasible / unknown, with one line of justification per cell.

all_of.note: DIAL 1 of 3 - 'every cell marked'. Computed as marked_cells / total_cells by the grid tool, which counts the cross-product itself; do NOT let a seat report this number.

DIAL 2 of 3 - the orthogonality proxy: 1 minus the maximum pairwise parameter correlation, produced by the parameterisation committee's independence check. Lower it only if you accept a weaker completeness claim.

any_of.note: DIAL 3 of 3 - an all-infeasible grid is a RESULT, not a failure. This branch is what stops the council forcing a pick out of an empty space.

metadata.title: Morphological grid council (12 seats - the only preset that may claim COMPLETENESS)
metadata.notes: WHEN TO USE: when the question is 'what are ALL the options' and someone will later rely on the answer being exhaustive - a requirements space, a config matrix, an interface surface. WHEN NOT TO USE: when the space is not enumerable (open-ended discovery - use C-X47) or when you need a ranked pick rather than a full map. The design's named dials are parameters and values. EDITABLE DIALS: /targets/categories (number of parameters/axes), /stopping/expression/any_of/0/all_of/1/value (the orthogonality bar), /participants/count/exact_n (cell evaluators scale with cell count, not with problem size), /budgets/time_minutes. STOPPING (human form): ALL[coverage_score >= 1, diversity_index >= 0.9] OR proof_of_impossibility == true. This spec was authored WITH stopping.source_expression - it needs no custom metric, so the SEM-001/SEM-012 collision does not apply - and SEM-001 rejected it anyway, because the reference parser emits no `note` key either: the schema's own inline-comment channel on a stop leaf is mutually exclusive with the human-readable source form. See _probe_sem_rule_collision.py case D. Per-dial notes were judged more valuable than the prose duplicate. PRESET-NAME CAVEAT: mapped to requirements_council because a morphological grid is the mechanism a requirements council uses to justify exhaustiveness; the competing reading is innovation_moonshot_council, which C-D38 takes. `preset` is itself a dial - change it if your use is not requirements work.
